# Migration source fixtures

These directories are frozen V1 projects, kept as migration input evidence
for the V2 design (`.savepoint/releases/v2/v2-Design.md` sections 1, 3, 9,
12). Each one is **byte-frozen**: never reformat, re-sync with current
templates, or "fix" its legacy vocabulary — a V1 project written years ago
looked exactly like this, and a future converter has to cope with it as-is.

A test that fails against one of these fixtures reports a compatibility
break in the reader or the migration path, not a stale fixture. Fix such a
failure by changing the code, or by making a deliberate, documented
migration decision — not by editing the file here.

Each fixture directory carries its own `manifest.yml`: a hand-authored,
manually reviewable inventory naming every source file, its exact-byte
SHA-256, and (for task files) the original scoped ID, raw status/phase, and
the expected completed/active classification. The hashes are established
once and are never regenerated by a test — see the comment at the top of
each `manifest.yml`.

| Fixture | Provenance |
| --- | --- |
| `v1-basic/` | A small, complete V1 project: one release, one epic, a completed baseline Task and a dependent in-progress Task still using the legacy `phase` field, an unknown nested metadata field, a body comment, multiline authored plan/evidence text, and CRLF line endings. No audit-register or Health-Check artifacts — their absence is the expected V1 shape. |
| `v1-history/` | A multi-release V1 project built on `v1-basic`'s helpers: the same epic (`E01-example`) and short Task ID (`T001-shared`) recur across release `v1` (done, resolved defect) and release `v1.1` (in progress, open defect of the same short ID), proving same-epic dependency resolution stays release-scoped. Adds a full `audit/` register — a fixed-but-unverified finding, an owner-waived finding, a finding explicitly marked duplicate of another, one immutable audit run, an epic audit, and a short custom `Health-Check.md` procedure. |

See `.gitattributes` in this directory for the rule that keeps these fixtures'
line endings byte-exact regardless of platform or `core.autocrlf`.
